label: Place
name: Bangladesh
summary:
Bangladesh, officially the People's Republic of Bangladesh, is a country in South Asia bordered by India on three sides and Myanmar to the southeast, with the Bay of Bengal forming its southern coastline. With 170 million people in 147,570 km², it is one of the world's most densely populated countries. Bangladesh occupies most of the Bengal delta — the world's largest river delta — formed by the confluence of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, making its geography defined by water, floods, and extraordinary agricultural fertility.

Historically part of the Bengal region, the territory experienced the 1947 Partition of India as East Pakistan — separated from West Pakistan by 1,600 km of Indian territory. The Language Movement of 1952 (in which students died defending the Bengali language against Urdu-only imposition) became the founding myth of Bangladeshi national identity. After West Pakistan's suppression of the 1970 election results won by the Awami League and the subsequent genocide of Bengalis (Operation Searchlight, 1971), Bangladesh declared independence in March 1971 with Indian military support. The 1971 Liberation War killed an estimated 300,000–3,000,000 people.

Bangladesh's economic transformation since the 1990s has been extraordinary. The garment industry — now 80% of export earnings — made Bangladesh the world's second-largest clothing exporter, lifting tens of millions out of poverty. The Rana Plaza factory collapse (2013, killing 1,134 workers) exposed the human cost of global supply chain economics. Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's increasingly authoritarian rule ended in August 2024 when student-led protests forced her into exile, initiating a new democratic transition.

causes: 1947 British India Partition creating East Pakistan — Bengali region separated from Hindu-majority India
Language Movement (1952) where Bangladeshi students died defending Bengali against Urdu imposition — creating the national identity kernel
1970 Awami League election victory suppressed by West Pakistan triggering the independence war
1971 Liberation War (Operation Searchlight) — Pakistani military genocide with Indian intervention enabling independence
effects: 1971 Liberation War — up to 3 million killed; one of the 20th century's largest mass atrocities
Bangladesh garment industry — world's second-largest clothing exporter; Rana Plaza (2013) becoming a symbol of global supply chain exploitation
2024 student revolution forcing Sheikh Hasina into exile — ending 15 years of authoritarian rule
Climate vulnerability — among the world's most threatened countries by sea-level rise and cyclones; 30% of land below 1m elevation
